subject: history
title: Civil War, Commonwealth and Restoration 1642-60
welcome_lead: From Edgehill to the return of Charles II.
meta_desc: OCR A-Level adventure on the English Civil War 1642-49, the Commonwealth under Cromwell and the Restoration 1660.
final_note: You can trace why Britain became (briefly) a republic and how monarchy was restored.

concepts.def: Conflict between Royalists (Cavaliers) and Parliamentarians (Roundheads) in three phases: 1642-46, 1648 (Second), 1649 settlement.
Reorganised Parliamentarian force created by the Self-Denying Ordinance and the February 1645 Act; led to victory at Naseby (June 1645).
Colonel Pride's 6 December 1648 exclusion of MPs unwilling to try the King, producing the Rump Parliament.
Charles I beheaded outside the Banqueting House, Whitehall, on 30 January 1649; monarchy and Lords abolished.
Oliver Cromwell ruled as Lord Protector 1653-58 under the Instrument of Government; succeeded briefly by his son Richard.
Return of Charles II following the Declaration of Breda (4 April 1660); entered London 29 May 1660.

walkthroughs.body_html: Charles raised his standard at Nottingham on 22 August 1642. Edgehill (October 1642) was inconclusive. The Solemn League and Covenant (1643) brought Scottish military help, decisive at Marston Moor (2 July 1644). The New Model Army won Naseby (14 June 1645). Charles surrendered to the Scots in May 1646.

Negotiations (the Heads of the Proposals, Newport) failed amid the Putney Debates (October-November 1647) and Charles's Engagement with the Scots. After the Second Civil War (1648), Pride's Purge produced the Rump. A High Court of Justice convicted Charles; he was beheaded on 30 January 1649. The Commonwealth was proclaimed; Cromwell's Irish (1649) and Scottish (1650-51) campaigns followed Worcester (3 September 1651).

Cromwell expelled the Rump in April 1653 and became Lord Protector under the Instrument of Government (December 1653). The Rule of the Major-Generals (1655-57) attempted godly reformation. The Humble Petition and Advice (1657) offered the crown, declined. Cromwell died 3 September 1658; instability under Richard, Lambert and the restored Rump led Monck to march south. The Declaration of Breda (April 1660) paved the way for Charles II's return.
